backup.production_rule: Guest guide v8.0.0 backend (s135), additive only: five tables guide_threads, guide_sessions, guide_messages, guide_auth_attempts, guide_events (RLS on, no policies, no grants to anon or authenticated); four guest RPCs (guide_session_v1, guide_thread_v1, guide_send_v1, guide_track_v1; anon and authenticated, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path empty); six staff RPCs (staff_guide_threads_v1, staff_guide_thread_v1, staff_guide_reply_v1, staff_guide_resolve_v1, staff_guide_usage_v1, staff_guide_guests_v1; authenticated only, gated by current_staff_authorized('manage_guest_inbox'); a missing thread id raises P0002 before the 42501 access check); the token helper and the push trigger function have no client and no service_role grant, guide_sweep_v1 is service_role only; no guide or staff guide function is executable by service_role except guide_sweep_v1 (no edge function calls them; the trigger runs without an execute check at fire time); trigger guide_messages_push on guide_messages calls notify-staff-inbox through pg_net and the vault secret and never fails the insert. guide_session_v1 refuses a booking whose name is a placeholder (reason no_name, no thread), keys its per-address throttle on cf-connecting-ip, else the rightmost x-forwarded-for entry (each trimmed and accepted only when address-shaped, ^[0-9A-Fa-f:.]{2,45}$), else the client id; x-real-ip and the leftmost x-forwarded-for entry are never used, allows 8 failures per address and 10 failures per check-in date per 15 minutes and 20 sessions per thread per day (reason busy), serialises mints per check-in date with an advisory lock whose wait is capped by a function-level lock_timeout of 2 s (a timeout answers reason busy and keeps nothing), and refuses a stay whose token would already be past its Manila expiry (reason expired, no session); answers a check-in date after Manila today + 3 with too_early and one before today - 90 with expired BEFORE any count, lock or insert (verify_booking not called, no attempt row); before any insert deletes up to 200 attempts older than 2 days (inline retention, index guide_auth_attempts_at_idx), so guide_auth_attempts holds at most about 185,000 rows (184240 by the formula; the window slides during the 48 h retention, adding under 1%), under 80 MB (asserted); guest messages are capped at 30 an hour and 200 per rolling 24 hours per thread (reason rate); guide_track_v1 caps events per device (600/hour, reason rate) and globally (60/minute and 1000 per rolling 24 hours, then drops silently: ok, stored 0) by arrival time, exactly (a batch is cut to the room left, no overshoot); it only tries its global advisory lock (pg_try_advisory_xact_lock) and drops the batch silently when the lock is busy, never waits; every call that gets the lock first deletes up to 200 events older than 30 days (inline retention, no scheduled job needed), so guide_events never holds more than 30000 rows; value is kept only up to 1e9 in size and rounded to 3 decimals (CHECK), meta keeps only whitelisted short scalar values and at most 200 bytes as stored (CHECK; a larger meta becomes {}); a search_empty event keeps the guest's single-token search term in target (max 80 chars) and the staff usage report shows it to staff; guide_sweep_v1 (optional housekeeping) deletes events older than 30 days, sessions 95 days after their expiry (the guests report needs them; an expired token is refused regardless) and sign-in attempts older than 2 days; staff_guide_usage_v1 answers only for the default property (single-property, other ids get an empty flagged object) and for at most 30 days (the retention); staff_guide_guests_v1(p_days, property) lists the guests who signed in to the guide (first name plus last initial only, last_seen within p_days clamped 1..90, newest first, 60 rows, total uncapped; default property only, other ids get {guests: [], total: 0, single_property: true}; event-based numbers cover the last 30 days; execute for authenticated only, service_role revoked, like every staff guide function); service_role has explicit full access to the five tables and the two identity sequences are closed to anon and authenticated. No existing table, function or setting is touched; verify_booking is called, not replaced. Phase is backfill, not expand, only because the body of guide_sweep_v1 contains DELETE FROM (housekeeping of the new tables), which release-safety refuses in an expand migration; the migration itself deletes no existing row and writes no data.
backup.notes: Apply after s134 and cf_confirm_flow (20261205000000) are applied; re-timed from 20261205000000 to 20261206000000 in s136 because cf_confirm_flow holds 20261205000000 live. The migration carries no begin/commit of its own (the runner wraps it). Restamp restore_point and verified_at with a fresh backup at apply time (scripts/migrations/fill-restore-point.mjs; the checker refuses one older than an hour). After the apply confirm notify-staff-inbox accepts {kind guest_wrote, psid guide:<uuid>} from the database caller, and run the post_apply_check. STORAGE (Free plan, one 500 MB database shared with bookings and the ledger): guide_events is bounded without any scheduled job. At most 1000 events are stored in any rolling 24 hours (60 a minute; both exact) and every guide_track_v1 call that gets the lock first deletes up to 200 events older than 30 days, so the table never holds more than 30000 rows. Measured in the rehearsal on a clone of the table (30000 rows, all four indexes, freshly loaded): worst case, every field at its maximum width (device 40, name 40, section 40, target 80, version 12 characters, value 12 digits, meta 200 stored bytes, thread id set, random device ids), 20,439,040 bytes = 19.5 MB (heap 14.6 MB, indexes 4.8 MB; 681 bytes a row), which is 3.9 % of the plan; typical events (36-character device id, short names, small meta, no thread id) 10,305,536 bytes = 9.8 MB at the full 30000 rows (343 bytes a row); a quiet guide of 300 events a day holds 9000 rows, about 3 MB. These are loaded sizes: dead rows and index pages between autovacuum runs can add to them for a while (at 1.5 times, 29 MB worst case). The pgTAP suite asserts under 30 MB and under 12 MB and that one more character or byte in any field is refused by the table. ACCEPTED LIMIT: the 1000 a day budget can be used up by anyone in about 20 minutes (the function is anonymous and device ids are client-chosen); analytics are then dropped silently for up to 24 hours (ok, stored 0). The guide, guest messages and sign-in are not affected; only usage numbers go missing. The orchestrator ruling of 2000 a day was halved because the full-width worst case measured 46.8 MB at 61470 rows (rehearsal r4), not well under 50 MB. guide_auth_attempts is bounded without a job as well. guide_session_v1 answers a check-in date outside [Manila today - 90, today + 3] before any count, lock or insert (too_early / expired, verify_booking not called, no row), and before any insert deletes up to 200 attempts older than 2 days, oldest first (index guide_auth_attempts_at_idx; the throttle windows are 15 minutes, so no older row is ever read). Rows kept are those of the last 2 days: failures are capped at 10 per check-in date in any 15 minutes (exact, under the per-date advisory lock), so at most 94 dates x 10 x 192 fifteen-minute windows = 180480 failure rows, plus ok rows (one per minted session; at most 20 sessions a thread a day, one thread per date: 94 x 20 x 2 = 3760): 184240 rows in all. Measured in the rehearsal on a clone of the table (184240 rows, every client at its full 80 characters and distinct, all four indexes, freshly loaded): 73867264 bytes = 70.4 MB (heap 24.8 MB, indexes 45.6 MB; about 400 bytes a row), 14 % of the plan; the pgTAP suite asserts under 80 MB. A realistic attacker stays far below it (one address is held to 8 failures per 15 minutes, 768 rows a day, all trimmed after 2 days); only an address-rotating attacker walking all 94 dates can reach it, and no further. Dead rows between autovacuum runs can add to the loaded size for a while. guide_messages: a guest can send 30 messages an hour and 200 in any rolling 24 hours per thread (reason rate), at most 2000 characters each; a thread exists only for a real booking and its session lives from three days before check-in to two days after checkout. Worst case for one hostile guest: 200 x about 2.3 KB (2000 ASCII characters plus row and index overhead) = about 0.46 MB a day per thread for ASCII text; with 4-byte characters (8 KB a message) about 1.6 MB a day, about 48 MB over a 30-night stay. The daily cap is count-then-insert without a lock, so parallel sends with one token can exceed 200 by the burst size; accepted (verified guests only, 30/h cap); a few stays at once (single property) add up to a few MB a day. There is no age trim on messages: they are the guest conversation and are kept. TRUSTED ROLES: service_role and the table owner insert into guide_events directly and bypass the track caps (trusted callers; no edge function does it). guide_sweep_v1 is optional housekeeping (weekly sweep or pg_cron job guide-sweep-weekly; it also trims guide_sessions and guide_auth_attempts); no storage bound depends on it. The Staff app Guide inbox and the guide v8.0.0 frontend follow the SQL. Guest-facing reasons and the post-apply check are listed under notes and post_apply_check.

forward_verification.name: guide_tables_present
forward_verification.query: select count(*) = 5 from pg_tables where schemaname = 'public' and tablename in ('guide_threads','guide_sessions','guide_messages','guide_auth_attempts','guide_events')

forward_verification.name: guide_rls_on_all_five
forward_verification.query: select bool_and(c.relrowsecurity) and count(*) = 5 from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and c.relname in ('guide_threads','guide_sessions','guide_messages','guide_auth_attempts','guide_events')

forward_verification.name: guide_anon_has_no_table_grants
forward_verification.query: select not exists (select 1 from information_schema.role_table_grants where grantee in ('anon','authenticated') and table_schema = 'public' and table_name like 'guide\_%')

forward_verification.name: guide_anon_may_not_call_staff_functions
forward_verification.query: select not bool_or(has_function_privilege('anon', f, 'execute')) from unnest(array['public.staff_guide_threads_v1(uuid)','public.staff_guide_thread_v1(uuid)','public.staff_guide_reply_v1(uuid,text,text)','public.staff_guide_resolve_v1(uuid,boolean)','public.staff_guide_usage_v1(integer,uuid)','public.staff_guide_guests_v1(integer,uuid)','public.guide_token_thread_v1(text)','public.guide_sweep_v1()']::regprocedure[]) f

forward_verification.name: guide_guests_report_authenticated_only
forward_verification.query: select has_function_privilege('authenticated', 'public.staff_guide_guests_v1(integer,uuid)', 'execute') and not has_function_privilege('anon', 'public.staff_guide_guests_v1(integer,uuid)', 'execute') and not has_function_privilege('service_role', 'public.staff_guide_guests_v1(integer,uuid)', 'execute')

forward_verification.name: guide_definer_functions_pin_search_path
forward_verification.query: select bool_and(p.proconfig @> array['search_path=""']) and count(*) >= 13 from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and (p.proname like 'guide\_%' or p.proname like 'staff\_guide\_%')

forward_verification.name: guide_push_trigger_present
forward_verification.query: select exists (select 1 from pg_trigger where tgname = 'guide_messages_push' and not tgisinternal)

forward_verification.name: guide_service_role_executes_only_the_sweep
forward_verification.query: select has_function_privilege('service_role', 'public.guide_sweep_v1()', 'execute') and (select not bool_or(has_function_privilege('service_role', f, 'execute')) from unnest(array['public.guide_session_v1(date,text,text,uuid)','public.guide_thread_v1(text,timestamptz)','public.guide_send_v1(text,text,text)','public.guide_track_v1(text,jsonb,text,text)','public.guide_token_thread_v1(text)','public.guide_messages_push_trg()','public.staff_guide_threads_v1(uuid)','public.staff_guide_thread_v1(uuid)','public.staff_guide_reply_v1(uuid,text,text)','public.staff_guide_resolve_v1(uuid,boolean)','public.staff_guide_usage_v1(integer,uuid)','public.staff_guide_guests_v1(integer,uuid)']::regprocedure[]) f)

forward_verification.name: guide_service_role_has_full_table_access
forward_verification.query: select bool_and(has_table_privilege('service_role', 'public.' || t, p)) from unnest(array['guide_threads','guide_sessions','guide_messages','guide_auth_attempts','guide_events']) t, unnest(array['select','insert','update','delete']) p

forward_verification.name: guide_identity_sequences_closed_to_clients
forward_verification.query: select not bool_or(has_sequence_privilege(r, 'public.' || q, p)) from unnest(array['anon','authenticated']) r, unnest(array['guide_auth_attempts_id_seq','guide_events_id_seq']) q, unnest(array['usage','select','update']) p

forward_verification.name: guide_events_width_checks_present
forward_verification.query: select count(*) = 2 from pg_constraint k where k.conrelid = 'public.guide_events'::regclass and k.contype = 'c' and (pg_get_constraintdef(k.oid) like '%pg_column_size(meta) <= 200%' or pg_get_constraintdef(k.oid) like '%round(value, 3)%')

post_apply_check: Throttle-key check, orchestrator PC, right after the apply. It WRITES: each of the two calls below inserts one row into public.guide_auth_attempts (two rows in all: failed sign-ins for a date inside the accepted window [Manila today - 90, today + 3] that has no booking; a date outside the window is answered without writing a row, so it cannot be used here; guide_session_v1 trims rows older than 2 days). Only the SELECT is read-only. Environment variable NAMES (values come from the password manager, never typed into a file): CASCADE_SUPABASE_URL (the project URL, https://<ref>.supabase.co) and CASCADE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (the publishable / anon key). Step 0, the test date D = Manila today - 80 days (a past date inside the window, so no arriving guest's per-date counter is touched), computed when you run it: bash: D=$(TZ=Asia/Manila date -d '-80 days' +%F) ; PowerShell: $D = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().AddHours(8).AddDays(-80).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd'). Use the same D in every step below (if D had a booking the answer may be expired instead of no_match: choose another past date between today - 90 and today - 4 with no booking). Step 1, the PC's real public IPv4: curl -4 -sS https://api.ipify.org . Step 2, a normal call: curl -4 -sS -X POST "$CASCADE_SUPABASE_URL/rest/v1/rpc/guide_session_v1" -H "apikey: $CASCADE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASCADE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"p_checkin_date":"<D>","p_initial":"Q","p_client":"zz-postapply-1"}' . Step 3, the same call with spoofed address headers: curl -4 -sS -X POST "$CASCADE_SUPABASE_URL/rest/v1/rpc/guide_session_v1" -H "apikey: $CASCADE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CASCADE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7" -H "CF-Connecting-IP: 203.0.113.7" -H "X-Real-IP: 203.0.113.7" -d '{"p_checkin_date":"<D>","p_initial":"Q","p_client":"zz-postapply-2"}' . (replace <D> with the date from step 0 in both bodies). Both answer {"ok": false, "reason": "no_match"}; if an answer is anything else, stop and repeat both calls with another date inside the window and in the SELECT. Step 4, read-only SQL (read-only runner): select client, ok, at from public.guide_auth_attempts where tried_date = date '<D>' order by at desc limit 2; PASS = two rows, both with ok false, and both clients equal ip:<the address from step 1>. FAIL, do not announce the guide: a row reads ip:203.0.113.7 (a caller can choose its own throttle key), or zz-postapply-1 / zz-postapply-2 (no address header reaches the database, the key is client-chosen and only the per-date cap of 10 protects), or both rows carry the same address that is not the PC's (a shared gateway address: all guests would share one counter of 8 failures per 15 minutes). In each FAIL case fix the key order by hotfix before announcing; messaging and the rest of the release are not affected.

guest_facing_reasons: throttled (guide_session_v1): 8 failed sign-ins from this address, or 10 failed sign-ins for this check-in date, in the last 15 minutes; checked first, so even the right initial is refused until the window passes.
no_name (guide_session_v1): the booking's name is a placeholder (Reserved / Airbnb / Not / empty), so any initial would match; no session is minted, the guest is pointed at Airbnb messaging.

busy (guide_session_v1): the stay's thread already has 20 sessions minted in the last 24 hours, or the call could not get its per-date lock within 2 seconds (many sign-ins for one date at once); nothing is kept, the guest tries again.

too_early (guide_session_v1): check-in is more than 3 days ahead (Manila); answered before verify_booking is called and without writing a row, so it says nothing about whether a booking exists; the answer carries opens_on = check-in minus 3.

expired (guide_session_v1): the check-in date is more than 90 days past (answered with no lookup and no row), or verify_booking says the stay is over (checkout + 1 day passed, UTC date), or the session's own expiry (Manila midnight of checkout + 2 days) has already passed.
session (guide_thread_v1, guide_send_v1): the token is unknown, malformed or past expires_at; the guide must sign in again.

rate (guide_send_v1): the guest sent 30 messages in the last hour, or 200 in the last 24 hours, on this thread (staff replies have their own cap of 60; guide_track_v1 also answers rate at 600 events an hour per device, and ok with stored 0 when the global 60 a minute or 1000 a day budget is used up or its lock is busy: all silent for the guest).
also: missing (blank initial), no_match (no booking or wrong initial), length (message empty or over 2000 characters), client_msg_id (outside 8 to 80 characters).
